How do you extract actionable intelligence from large, messy datasets?

Intelligence extraction workflow: 1) Data quality audit first: missing values distribution, obvious errors, duplicate records, unexpected value ranges. In pandas: df.info(), df.describe(), df.isnull().sum(), df.duplicated().sum(). Fix before analysis — garbage in, garbage out. 2) Univariate analysis: distribution of each variable, outliers. Box plots, histograms, violin plots. 3) Bivariate analysis: correlations between variables. Heatmap of Pearson correlations. Scatter matrices. For categorical: chi-square test, Cramér's V. 4) Temporal analysis if time series: trend, seasonality, anomalies, changepoints (Prophet, PELT changepoint detection). 5) Segmentation: k-means, DBSCAN, or hierarchical clustering to identify natural groups in data. Validate with silhouette scores. 6) Anomaly detection: IsolationForest, LOF (Local Outlier Factor), statistical methods (z-score > 3, IQR method). 7) Hypothesis testing: define question → formulate null hypothesis → select appropriate test (t-test, ANOVA, Mann-Whitney, chi-square) → interpret p-value AND effect size. 8) Visualization for communication: bar charts for comparison, line charts for trends, scatter for relationships, maps for geographic. Intelligence is the so what — not what happened but why it happened and what to do about it.

What are the principles of good data visualization and how do you make charts that communicate clearly?

Edward Tufte's principles: Data-ink ratio — maximize ink used to convey data, minimize decorative ink. Remove chartjunk: unnecessary gridlines, 3D effects, redundant encoding. Every pixel should earn its place. Small multiples: same chart type, same scale, showing different slices — allows comparison without cognitive overhead. Clear hierarchy: most important information should be visually dominant. Alberto Cairo's truthful, functional, beautiful, insightful, enlightening framework. Perceptual accuracy by encoding type: position (most accurate), length, angle (less accurate), area, volume, color (least accurate for quantitative). Use color purposefully: categorical (qualitative palette — colorblind safe: ColorBrewer), sequential (one-variable continuous), diverging (centered around meaningful midpoint). Avoid: dual Y-axis (almost always misleading — suggests relationship), pie charts (angle comparison is imprecise — use bar), 3D charts (depth distortion), truncated Y-axis starting non-zero (distorts magnitude). Instead: always start at zero for bar charts (or make clear if not), use connected dot plot for before/after, slope chart for two-point comparison. Annotation > legend: label data directly where possible rather than forcing legend lookup. Test: show to someone unfamiliar with the data — what conclusions do they draw in 5 seconds?
